children: shares traded nearly 5% lower at around $41.80 in premarket trading Monday, despite CEO Daniel Roberts highlighting continued strength in AI compute demand and constraints on supply.
In a recent X post, Roberts said concerns over slowing the pace of frontier AI development should be separated from the existing demand for compute.
He argued that even if AI models stopped improving today, deploying their current capabilities would require more compute than the industry can build for years.
Roberts pointed to comments from Anthropic
CEO Dario Amodei, who said in May that the company had planned for 10x growth but was running at an 80x pace in the first quarter, creating challenges in securing compute.
President Greg Brockman also said in July that the company expects to remain compute-constrained and is choosing which products to scale.
, meanwhile, has said it is processing 7x more tokens than a year ago, Roberts noted, adding that demand rises again as new compute capacity comes online.

On the supply side, he also identified high-bandwidth memory (HBM) as a key constraint for AI chips, as the three companies producing HBM are sold out for the year, while new memory capacity can take years to build.
Roberts also cited TrendForce estimates for 50%-60% HBM shipment growth next year and said NVIDIA
, the largest HBM buyer, expects roughly 70% revenue growth next year while describing its outlook as supply-constrained.
Beyond chips and memory, the CEO said building data centers and connecting them to power takes even longer. Citing Goldman Sachs
in the post, he said only about half of U.S. capacity scheduled over the next two years is expected to be built on time.
“Demand continues to seem heavily weighted to the upside,” Roberts said, while supply risks remain tilted toward less capacity being built rather than more.

title: Iren Falls 5% in premarket as CEO sees AI compute supply crunch
